about: Wave M5 S4 (docs/scale/M5_DESIGN.md 5, "As built: the export file"): the till's rescue file. Read by the PHP test (backend/tests/Unit/PosSync/SyncExportVectorsTest.php) and by the Dart test of pos_sync. Generated once by an independent script (Python hmac/hashlib/json), never by the code under test.

format.file: UTF-8 text without a BOM; every line is one JSON object written without spaces or line breaks and ends with LF (never CRLF). Line 1 the header, then `count` body lines, then the trailer as the last line.
format.header: Keys in this order: format ("rizqim-sync-export"), version (1), device (the uuid of the till that writes the file, lower case), kid (the number of the key the file mac is made with), kids (the kid of every signed body line, each once, ascending), first_seq and last_seq (the lowest and highest seq of the header device's own lines; null when it has none), count (the number of body lines), created_at (UTC, ISO 8601). A reader ignores keys it does not know.
format.body: One operation per line, as POST /pos/sync takes it: a signed one {"signed","mac","prev","kid"} with the journal's text, mac, prev and kid unchanged (never signed again); an unsigned one as the operation itself {"op_id","seq","type","occurred_at","staff_id","payload"[,"origin_device"]}. An operation queued under another pairing (a queue set aside, its device uuid is not the header's) carries that uuid in lower case as a last key "dev". Order: lines with dev first (by dev as text, then seq, then op_id), then the device's own lines (by seq, then op_id). One line per op_id.
format.trailer: {"file_mac":"<64 lower-case hex>"} = HMAC-SHA256(key, utf8(file_label) || every byte of the file before the trailer line), i.e. the header line and the body lines, each with its LF. The key is the header device's key number `kid`. A LF after the trailer is written; a reader takes the file without it too.
format.json: As Dart jsonEncode writes it: no spaces, keys in the order given, only the quote, the backslash and characters below U+0020 escaped (\n, \r, \t, \b, \f, else \u00XX), / and non-ASCII left as they are.
format.limits: At most 8 MiB and 10 000 body lines per file.

test_keys.about: No key is written here. key(device, kid) = HMAC-SHA256(key = utf8(seed), data = utf8(lowercase(device) + "/kid-" + kid)), 32 bytes; a test derives them.

files.name: one till, five signed operations
files.about: The till's own queue under key 1, given out of order. The builder writes them in seq order.

files.name: two keys and an unsigned line
files.about: Operations queued under key 1, one queued unsigned, then two under key 2 after a rotation. The file is under key 2 (the header kid); kids lists the keys of the signed lines.

files.name: a queue set aside before the till was paired again
files.about: Lines of the earlier pairing (another device uuid, its own key 3: signed under it, never re-signed) carry dev and come first; first_seq and last_seq count the header device's own lines only. An own line given with dev equal to the header device (any letter case) is written without dev.

files.name: nothing waiting
files.about: An empty queue: no body line, first_seq and last_seq null, kids empty.

readers.about: Texts made from files[0] and what a reader says of each under key(device, 1): ok, or the reason it refuses the whole file with.

cases.name: without the line break after the trailer
one character of a body line changed
a version this reader does not know (the mac is right)
another format name (the mac is right)
not a file of this kind
